macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Asian stocks slip as AI concerns weigh; U.S. futures recover
items.summary: Asian shares traded lower as investors questioned the sustainability of heavy artificial-intelligence investment, following a sharp October selloff in technology stocks. U.S. futures edged higher, with S&P 500 futures up about 0.4% and Nasdaq 100 futures up about 0.6%.[1]

items.title: Nasdaq suffers worst month since April 2025
items.summary: The Nasdaq fell nearly 7% in October, while Friday’s session saw the Nasdaq 100 drop 3.5% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunge 7.2%. Investors are focusing on whether weaker technology valuations and a broader stock selloff could affect the Federal Reserve’s December policy decision.[1][7]

items.title: Markets reassess prospects for a December Fed rate hike
items.summary: Markets still imply roughly a 72% probability of a quarter-point Federal Reserve rate increase in December, although the amount of additional tightening priced into futures has declined from more than 70 basis points to about 55 basis points.[1]

items.title: China shifts toward daily overnight-rate operations
items.summary: The People’s Bank of China began daily overnight reverse-repurchase operations at a fixed 1.25% rate, below its 1.4% seven-day rate. The move brings China’s framework closer to an overnight-rate operating system used by the Federal Reserve, ECB and Bank of Japan.[2]

items.title: Apple, Palantir and Berkshire Hathaway earnings due
items.summary: Apple, Palantir Technologies and Berkshire Hathaway are scheduled to report during the week, with Apple’s results expected after Monday’s market close. Advanced Micro Devices is scheduled to report Tuesday, while investors are also watching upcoming jobs data and U.S. midterm elections.[3][8]

items.title: China regulators meet financial firms to support stocks
items.summary: Chinese financial regulators are expected to meet banks and securities firms to discuss measures supporting the capital market, as authorities seek to stabilize Chinese equities after recent weakness.[7]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rises 1% as Binance transfers 7,499 BTC from SAFU
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $78,354, up about 1% over 24 hours, while Ethereum rose 0.9% to roughly $2,275. Binance completed a transfer of 7,499 BTC, worth approximately $581 million, from its Secure Asset Fund for Users.

items.title: Binance resumes withdrawals after $6.3 billion hack
items.summary: Binance restored withdrawals across multiple networks after a security attack that reportedly caused $6.3 billion in losses. The exchange experienced substantial outflows, including about $3.6 billion after withdrawals resumed.

items.title: Crypto market sees more than $130 million in liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin traded between approximately $77,600 and $78,500 as investors assessed the Binance hack. More than $130 million in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, while total market capitalization declined about 0.5%.

items.title: USDC Treasury mints $250 million on Solana
items.summary: The USDC Treasury minted 250 million USDC on Solana, increasing the supply of the dollar-backed stablecoin on the network by approximately $250 million.

items.title: North Korea-linked address moves $38 million through Relay bridge
items.summary: A blockchain investigator identified more than $38 million transferred through the Relay cross-chain bridge from an address linked to North Korea. Relay said transaction monitoring was enabled, while the transfers remained under investigation.

items.title: SOON suspends svmBNB bridge after abnormal withdrawals
items.summary: The SOON Foundation temporarily closed the bridge between svmBNB and the SOON mainnet after detecting abnormal withdrawal activity. The bridge was placed under control and an investigation began.

items.title: Threshold Network pauses tBTC minting and redemption
items.summary: Threshold Network suspended tBTC minting and redemption while addressing Linux kernel vulnerability CVE-2026-98432. The network said reserves remained sufficient and no unauthorized minting or Bitcoin transfers had been detected.

items.title: THORChain restores solvency after erroneous 10 ETH payment
items.summary: THORChain temporarily halted Ethereum-related activity after a single-block reorganization triggered an erroneous 10 ETH payout. The user returned the funds, and the vault regained solvency.

items.title: Hyperliquid plans HYPE token repurchases
items.summary: Hyperliquid is expected to generate more than $15 million in November reserve earnings and use part of the proceeds to repurchase approximately 180,000 HYPE tokens.

items.title: RDUSD stablecoin planned for HSK Chain
items.summary: Yuanbi Technology announced plans to deploy its U.S. dollar stablecoin RDUSD on HSK Chain. The parties said they would explore cross-border payments, fund management, and real-world asset tokenization.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: AI model releases and claims dominate industry news
items.summary: Reports say OpenAI and Anthropic have unveiled or internally tested next-generation models, while other coverage highlights Google Genie 4, Mistral Large 4, and Inception Mercury 3. Several claims come from newsletters and secondary reports and require confirmation from official announcements.

items.title: AI cybersecurity becomes a major commercial focus
items.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic are positioning AI systems as tools for finding and fixing software vulnerabilities, while OpenAI finance chief Sarah Friar described cybersecurity as a potentially major business opportunity. The trend reflects growing concern about AI-assisted hacking and defensive automation.

items.title: Mistral reportedly open-sources Large 4 model
items.summary: A machine-learning industry newsletter reports that Mistral Large 4, described as a one-trillion-parameter multimodal mixture-of-experts model, is now available with open weights and multiple reasoning modes.

items.title: Enterprise AI spending shifts toward cheaper models
items.summary: Coverage reports that SAP is moving some workloads to less expensive AI models and expects more than €2 billion in efficiency gains over two years. Separate industry estimates point to falling token prices alongside sharply higher AI usage.

items.title: AI-generated virtual worlds emerge as a competitive frontier
items.summary: Reports describe Google Genie 4 as a system that generates explorable environments from text prompts or images, with interactive characters and generated audio. The development highlights increasing competition around world models and multimodal simulation.
